Firearms training is one thing, but medic training is something you do not want to get online if you can help it at all. Sure, get the skills and read all you can, but using said skills IRL without the certs can get you in hot water. And of course, it's a good idea to know what to do if you have to save yourself or someone close to you.

As for firearms training, a lot of the stuff you'll find online that's been around for a while is long outdated. For instance, in the 70-80's, some manuals recommended that you should start firing center mass and all your follow-up shots go progressively lower. The idea behind this is that you're "following" your target to the ground as they take fire. Of course, this is retarded for obvious reasons, but I know of two instructors that still unironically teach this today. They're both boomer fudds running CCW mills.

With that out of the way, the Magpul Dynamics series is a decent start. Anything from Massad Ayoob will help you with the legal side, and Paul Harrell's stuff is interesting. This guy is pretty dope too: https://yewtu.be/channel/UCl1a1FOUwxh5pOsGOZw37Cg

Finally, remember that IRL training is harder to get the better it is (generally speaking). The classes run by former operators and spooks will often require background checks, to make sure they're not training the "wrong" folks. Look for those wherever you are, a lot of them will often have cushy private facilities. Make a vacation of it -- spending $5k to fly to a private range and training with a bunch of SOCOM boys is a helluva lot better than spending that same amount drinking at some tourist trap.
